source_resources.prerequisites: Python, PyTorch, and Day 46-48 Transformer model architecture.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Compact historical code reference for the named implementation functions; CS336 spring2025 provides the lead component exercises. Do not infer top-p, atomic persistence or cloud budget enforcement from nanoGPT.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: train.py: training loop (while True): forward under ctx, scaler.scale(loss).backward(), clip_grad_norm_(grad_clip), scaler.step(optimizer)
source_resources.known_availability_limitations: Historical implementation reference: nanoGPT README marks the repository deprecated (November 2025). Toy CPU reading/runs do not establish full GPU pretraining feasibility.

source_resources.title: Decoupled Weight Decay Regularization
source_resources.author: Ilya Loshchilov, Frank Hutter
source_resources.permission_basis: Lawful academic citation and reference under arXiv open access terms; no paper figures or prose reproduced.
source_resources.prerequisites: Stochastic gradient descent, L2 regularization, and momentum concepts from Days 31-33.
source_resources.selection_rationale: Foundational primary literature defining AdamW, demonstrating that L2 regularization does not equal decoupled weight decay in adaptive gradient algorithms.
source_resources.safe_fallback: All update equations and mathematical proofs are self-contained in the curriculum lessons.

compared_candidates.candidate_name: Kingma & Ba: Adam: A Method for Stochastic Optimization (2014)
compared_candidates.comparison_rationale: Original Adam algorithm implementing L2 regularization via gradient addition, leading to sub-optimal generalization compared to decoupled weight decay.
Standard library reference; Loshchilov & Hutter provides theoretical mathematical derivations and empirical justification.

source_resources.relevant_timestamp: Section 2 Decoupling the Weight Decay from the Gradient-Based Update (Algorithm 2, AdamW)
